content.value_statement: WebSocket features often fail from missed heartbeats, weak reconnection, or unvalidated messages. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for stable real-time connections.
actual_capabilities: Shows a WebSocket server pattern that shares an HTTP server port.
Provides a heartbeat loop using ping, pong, and connection termination.
Demonstrates client reconnection with exponential backoff.
Shows typed message handling with JSON parsing and validation.
Includes a checklist for reviewing WebSocket reliability.
limitations: Does not provide a complete WebSocket framework or package.
Does not cover authentication, authorization, or rate limiting.
Does not include production deployment or scaling guidance.
Examples need adaptation for each runtime and library version.

use_cases.title: Add Server Heartbeats
use_cases.description: Use the server pattern to keep idle WebSocket connections healthy and close stale clients.

use_cases.title: Improve Client Reconnection
use_cases.description: Use the reconnection pattern to recover from dropped connections with capped exponential backoff.

use_cases.title: Review Real-Time Code
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to inspect heartbeat, reconnect, validation, and error handling coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic WebSocket Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a WebSocket server and client for my real-time feature. Include heartbeat, reconnection, and message validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a new WebSocket feature

prompt_templates.title: Add Heartbeat Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my WebSocket server design and suggest a heartbeat approach using ping and pong. Explain where stale connections should close.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Dropped Connections
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect why my WebSocket client disconnects often. Focus on reconnect timing, error logging, and server heartbeat behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Production WebSocket Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my WebSocket architecture for reliability gaps. Check server setup, heartbeat cadence, reconnection backoff, and message validation.

output_examples.input: Review my WebSocket server heartbeat design.
output_examples.output: The review identifies missing pong tracking, recommends a 30-second heartbeat, and explains when stale clients should be terminated.

output_examples.input: Help me improve reconnect behavior for a browser client.
output_examples.output: The response recommends capped exponential backoff, resets attempts after a successful open event, and logs connection errors for diagnosis.

output_examples.input: Check whether my message handler is safe enough.
output_examples.output: The response asks for typed message validation, graceful invalid-message responses, and explicit handling for supported message types.

best_practices: Validate every received message before processing it.
Use capped exponential backoff for client reconnection.
Track heartbeat state and close stale connections promptly.
anti_patterns: Leaving dead connections open without ping and pong checks.
Retrying reconnects with no delay or maximum interval.
Processing parsed messages without checking expected types.

faq.question: Does this skill execute WebSocket code?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and example patterns that users adapt to their projects.

faq.question: Which WebSocket problems does it target?
faq.answer: It targets server setup, heartbeat handling, client reconnection, message validation, and dropped-connection debugging.

faq.question: Can it replace a WebSocket library?
faq.answer: No. It helps design and review implementations, but it does not provide a runtime library.

faq.question: Does it cover security controls?
faq.answer: It covers message validation basics, but it does not cover authentication, authorization, or abuse prevention in depth.

faq.question: Is it useful for TypeScript projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use TypeScript-style snippets for server, client, and message-handling patterns.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it for reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude Code and Codex can use it to inspect WebSocket reliability patterns in a project.
